openings.claim: Test necessity of rod-matched, close-fitting four-face enclosure: neither tight-fit/outcome implication is established; two tighter-fit trials returning 3 mm farther motivate removal only. Replace aperture dependence with fixed two-face plywood datums, insertion stops and offcut pressure shoes; hand-adjusted bolts seat rods against datums with opposing-face clearance. Keep bolts/nuts engaged; elastic loops/cord retain shoes.
openings.discriminator: Unchanged datums and seating pressure may recover position across 19-to-18 mm substitution without aperture refitting. Rival: greater clamp restraint explains success. Equal return with loaded displacement improving only under increased pressure supports that rival; improved unloaded clearance return at comparable pressure while sustaining load supports aperture removal.
openings.probe: Within 100 fabrication minutes, build two settings of one joint: ordinary close fit and opposing-face clearance, preserving datums. Use only supplied stock/tools, hand assembly/adjustment, drill plywood only; no rod drilling, adhesive or permanent marks. Verify 90 mm cube envelope and attachment throughout withdrawal. Ruler/fixed bolt-turn procedure approximates comparable seating pressure. Within 20 testing minutes, run ten alternating exchanges/configuration, five/rod; substitute 18 mm for smaller rod’s last two. Log time/return; four 10 N, ten-second load trials/configuration. Reject any exchange reaching forty seconds, return/load outside 2 mm circle, detached hardware or permanent rod marks. Inability to fabricate captive shoes or finish measurements within resources defeats probe without establishing necessity.
openings.uncertainty: Pressure equality remains unknown; supplied plywood/hardware may not provide sufficiently rigid captive datums within envelope. Unmeasured clamping capacity may fail load or mark rods. No performance demonstrated.

lineage.reason: Retains aperture-removal relation, both rival comparisons, declared uncertain fit, assumptions and fabrication/testing defeat conditions.

decision: Retain one bounded fabrication counterexample candidate; test within resource limits. Success remains unproven and provides no deployment authorization.
